title: Flying Squirrels Secretly Glow Hot Pink Under UV Light
subject: flying squirrel

scenes.text: Shine a purple flashlight on a flying squirrel. It glows pink.
A Wisconsin professor spotted it at a bird feeder, with a UV flashlight.
His team checked 135 squirrel skins in museums. Nearly every flying squirrel glowed. Gray, fox and red squirrels didn't.
Before that, the only mammals known to do this were opossums.
Why do they glow? Nobody knows. Maybe to find each other in the dark, or to confuse predators.
Museum skins from the 1800s glow too. It was always there, waiting for the right flashlight.

description:
Shine an ultraviolet flashlight on a flying squirrel and it glows bright pink.
Researchers at Northland College in Wisconsin checked 135 squirrel skins in museum collections. Nearly all of the flying squirrels fluoresced, including specimens collected in the 1800s, while gray, fox and red squirrels did not. Why they glow is still unknown.
What do you think the glow is for?
first_comment: Scientists still haven't tested flying squirrels from other parts of the world. Which animal do you think we're missing a hidden glow in?
